thread:
alice: Quick heads-up — I ran the int3/deep-quant bringup for orion48k against the long-context harness and hit a divergence between quantized KV and FP baseline around token ~32768. KV hit looks like a wrap/phase mismatch, not simple bit noise. Posting small repro log below.

bryan: Can you drop the minimal repro command and a tiny log snippet? :eyes:

alice: Sure — here's the command I used and the failing tail of the comparison output:

```
# run on staging-gpu-12, model=orion48k, quant=int3
./run_eval --model orion48k --quant int3 --eval-set longprefill_10k.json --max-tokens 35000 --seed 42

# diff at token 32769
KV mismatch: idx=32769, fp_val=0.000214, q_val=0.000000
logit_delta: 7.2e-2, top1-mismatch true
```

cheng: That smells like RoPE phase wrap at the new window boundary — orion48k extends rotary to 48k, we didn't adjust posscale clamping in the int3 path. Could also be quantized rot-mul error when index > 32768.

sara: Can you also run an int4 and int8 comparison (same prefix) so we know if it's strictly an int3 quant artifact or general at-large-context issue? I'll spin up the harness for int4 now.

alice: Launching int4/int8 now. Quick plan: 1) prefill-only compare (no streaming) 2) streaming step-by-step token compare 3) dump KV tensors at boundary

bryan: Good. Also add a tiny targeted test that forces positions around 32760-32780 with deterministic prompt (shorter run) so we don't wait for full 35k.

eval-bot: Automated run created: https://ci.internal/runs/ORION-quant-3234567891 — int3 vs fp baseline quick-prefill + kv-dump. Quick metrics: divergence-first-token=32769, KL_delta_window=0.184, perplexity_ratio=1.22.

alice: Results from prefill-only quick test (prefill deterministic prompt around the boundary): majority of tokens match until 32768, then sharp mismatch. Inline snippet of token ids where mismatch begins:

```
... 32765 32766 32767 32768 32769 32770 ...
FP_next_ids: 198 77  9   45   12   102
Q_next_ids: 198 77  9   45   0    102
```

sara: Hmm zeroing at 32769 in the quant path. Looks like a saturation/overflow handling maybe kicks in when pos index wraps or when rotary sin/cos table lookup crosses 32768 boundary. :thinking:

cheng: Two quick checks: 1) confirm posscale clamp/scale factors in quant kernel for rot-mul; 2) inspect memcpy/alignment when we copy KV shards (int3 packing can shift byte offsets). I've seen a similar symptom when a 16-byte alignment assumption is violated.

bryan: I'll bisect recent commits touching rotary, posenc, and quant packer. If someone can give me the exact commit range used for the failing build that helps.

alice: Build metadata: commit range build: origin/main@{2026-03-18..2026-03-21}, docker image sha: sha256:8f3c...45ab. Sending to the triage issue.

sara: I kicked off int4 and int8 runs — int4 shows a smaller KL jump at same token (0.038) and int8 is basically fine. So severity correlates with quant level.

alice: I'm going to run: `./bench/kv_check --model orion48k --quant int3 --posscale-clamp 1e-3 --seed 42 --positions 32760-32780` and also dump raw rot-cos/sin values at those positions. Will share outputs in 20m.

eval-bot: Quick note — bench harness logs are at: https://logs.internal/orion/3234567891 (kv-dumps + small visual diff).

alice: Pasted rot-cos values: at pos=32769 the quant kernel loaded cos=0.0 (quantized packing shows a zero block), while FP baseline cos=0.71234. So kernel's table read seems wrong post-index wrap.

cheng: If cos is zeroed after index, that explains the zero token output. Likely index -> byte-offset math bug when index exceeds 32768 and we apply a mask for packing words. I'll run a microtest on the packer math now.

bryan: Opening GH issue ORION-1234 with links to CI and logs. Assign alice for further repro artifacts, cheng to debug packer, me to bisect.

sara: Plan: alice runs expanded eval across int3/int4/int8 overnight and attaches full kv dumps; cheng to validate packer alignment and posscale clamp; bryan will bisect and propose rollback candidate if quick fix not found.

alice: Yep — kicking off the long sweep now. ETA ~6h. Will update the thread with artifacts and a minimal reproducer script.

bryan: Thanks — please add a short reproducible test that we can run in CI (prefill-only, deterministic seed, <1s runtime) so we can catch regressions in presubmit.

alice: Will do. :thumbsup:
